title: Equilibrium expression Kp (and Qp) for gas-phase reactions

items.label: K_p
items.meaning: equilibrium constant written in terms of partial pressures (Q_p has the same form at any time; at equilibrium K_p = Q_p)

items.label: P_C
items.meaning: partial pressure of gaseous product C

items.label: c
items.meaning: stoichiometric coefficient of C in the balanced equation aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD (exponent on P_C)

items.label: P_D
items.meaning: partial pressure of gaseous product D

items.label: d
items.meaning: stoichiometric coefficient of D in the balanced equation (exponent on P_D)

items.label: P_A
items.meaning: partial pressure of gaseous reactant A

items.label: a
items.meaning: stoichiometric coefficient of A in the balanced equation (exponent on P_A)

items.label: P_B
items.meaning: partial pressure of gaseous reactant B

items.label: b
items.meaning: stoichiometric coefficient of B in the balanced equation (exponent on P_B)

caution: Written for the reaction aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD. Substances whose concentrations or partial pressures are independent of the amount, such as solids and pure liquids, are not included in the expression. Conversion between Kc and Kp will not be assessed on the AP Exam, but pay attention to whether Kc or Kp is used in a question.
ced_evidence: 7.3.A.1 "for (Kp, Qp)" equilibrium expression Kp = (PC)^c (PD)^d / (PA)^a (PB)^b; 7.3.A.2 "does not include substances whose concentrations (or partial pressures) are independent of the amount, such as for solids and pure liquids"
